Circa 1920s-30s - Length: 2-3/4”
The Cap & Barrel: The engraving reads "18KT - 1/10 GOLD FILLED". This indicates a high-grade manufacturing process where a thick layer of solid 18-karat gold is mechanically bonded to a base metal core. In the 1920s, a 1/10 fractional ratio was exceptionally generous, meaning 10% of the total overlay metal's weight is true gold (more common vintage pens often used a thinner 1/20 ratio).\n• The Nib: The stamp confirms it is a solid 14-karat gold nib. Nibs from this era especially those coming from former Waterman craftsmen are highly celebrated among modern collectors for their impressive smoothness and flexible expression.
